score_meanings.promise_vocabulary: 0 drifts into claims/profiles/central trust-ledger framing, 5 stays promise-first and pCID-specific
score_meanings.simplicity_durability: 0 overbuilt or fragile, 5 minimal, durable, and small-device-friendly under the 100-year goal

promise_theory_rules: A promise is a scoped declaration of intent.
No agent can make a promise on behalf of another agent.
Trust is a local assessment of whether a promise will be kept.
Promises to receive or use are not equivalent to obligations, impositions, or promises to give.
promise_theory_references: Mark Burgess, In Search of Certainty
Mark Burgess, Promise Theory: Principles and Applications

assessment.rationale: Useful envelope mechanics for carrying signed evidence, but this specimen does not directly model a kept storage promise or Bob's local promise-accounting record. It is technically plausible and fairly auditable, yet its promise vocabulary is weak because the crucial outer conformance claim is not expressed as an agent-scoped promise.
strengths: Deterministic CBOR arrays make artifacts compact and auditable.
Clear separation between outer layer protocol and actual payload protocol.
Unknown-pCID policy avoids false claims when handlers are missing.
Nested signature over [pcid_b, payload_b] improves payload/protocol binding.
weaknesses: Does not define storage-promise semantics or Bob's local accounting record.
Promise wording is not agent-first; a pCID/protocol is described as promising behavior.
Unsigned outer envelope weakens authorship and auditability of the conformance claim.
risks: Bob may be unable to attribute who promised that payload_a conforms to pcid_a if transport context is lost or replayed.
A valid nested signature can authenticate payload_b while leaving the outer layer's semantics disputable.
Scenario coverage is weak because storage-duration, retrieval outcome, and local accounting semantics are absent.
open_questions: Can the nested signed payload be used to carry explicit agent-scoped storage promises and later kept/failed observations without depending on transport identity?
Does the outer envelope need its own signature or signer reference so Bob can attribute the conformance promise locally?
What minimal payload schema would let Bob record 'Alice served chunk C after promising to keep it' in promise-first terms?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; evaluates this envelope specimen against storage-promise accounting pressure and does not settle canonical PromiseGrid design.

autonomous_agents.note: The design does not impose central control and leaves trust decisions to peers, but it under-specifies which agent makes the outer conformance promise.

scoped_intent.note: Intent is clear for parsing and signature coverage, but not clearly scoped as 'Alice promises ...' for the outer envelope conformance claim.

no_promises_for_others.note: The text attributes a promise to pcid_a/the protocol layer instead of a concrete agent, which drifts from promise-first agent wording.

no_guaranteed_outcomes.note: The draft does not guarantee successful interpretation or delivery; unsupported handlers must withhold claims.

local_trust_assessment.note: Trust is explicitly local via transport identity or peer-adoption records, but the unsigned outer layer makes that assessment weak and context-dependent.

accept_use_not_obligation.note: The draft does not collapse receipt or use into obligation semantics.

violations: Outer conformance is framed as a property of pcid_a/layer semantics rather than an explicit autonomous agent promise.
Unsigned outer envelope leaves authorship of the conformance promise ambiguous and too dependent on transport context.
